societies.name: Stellaris — Human Bio-Trophies under Rogue Servitors
societies.society: A modeled machine empire maintaining human organics under Mandatory Pampering

scope.continuity: Released Synthetic Dawn Rogue Servitor scenario; qualitative rules only
scope.period: A functioning player-configured empire with supplied organic sanctuaries
scope.population: Living human organic Bio-Trophies in the chosen configuration
exclusions: Alien species silently added to the human denominator
Shortage or extermination states as identical provision
scope.branch: Rogue Servitor empire with human organics and Mandatory Pampering

societies.description:
Rogue Servitors turn organic maintenance into the purpose of a machine economy. In this explicitly modeled human configuration, robots run production while human residents receive sanctuary life and the Mandatory Pampering standard. The material guarantee estimate is strong within a functioning, supplied empire; it is a rule-based arrangement rather than a claim that the player cannot cause shortages or lose a war. The sources describe the qualitative system across versions, while obsolete launch-era balance numbers are deliberately omitted.

Control lies with the machine intelligence, which frees its charges from responsibility while also removing agency. Affection, high happiness and a species-rights interface weight do not establish human ownership of the productive system. A high nonworking estimate follows the explicitly pampered life and delegation of ordinary production, but remains broad because useful art, care or other cultural activity can continue. The game’s Unity output is not automatically either a real job or proof of pure idleness. Only the selected living human population forms the denominator; robot drones do not inflate it.

guarantees.basis: Mandatory Pampering and supplied sanctuaries organize continuing support; the scope assumes a functioning economy, not immunity to player-induced shortages.

control.basis: Machine administration removes organic productive responsibility and agency; interface political weights are not human ownership.

nonworking.basis: Pampered organics delegate ordinary production, but useful chosen cultural activity may continue and Unity is an abstract resource, not a census.

evidence.claim: The released scenario lets machines maintain organic Bio-Trophies under compulsory pampering without ordinary productive responsibility.
evidence.locator: Official DLC announcement; citizenship/living-standard tables and presentation notes

uncertainties: A player-configured human case, not a single fixed canonical civilization.
Qualitative rules only; no current patch-specific numerical claims.
Unity does not determine useful-work participation.
Supply failures and other organic statuses are separate modeled states.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

review_notes: Twelve fast decisions and one explicitly configurable Rogue Servitor record. No complete game, novel or patch-history read.
Official Synthetic Dawn release context corroborates clearly labeled public rules references. Current official wiki access failed and was not bypassed.
No obsolete launch-era balance numbers or new sequel promises were adopted. Machine workers, biological cyborg workers and maintained organics remain different cases.
Atomic Heart’s promised full post-labor rollout and closing control struggle do not establish a settled future economy.
The Uncertain’s advertised extinction is treated as a premise, and SteamWorld’s surviving human Shiners are not erased.
